en_US.title: Pump Room Handshake
en_US.scanner: The pump room is the first honest machine: if the player cannot read intake, output and failure noise, the room is useless.
en_US.field_note: The room only works when the safe path and the flooding path share the same hardware.
en_US.terminal: Pump handshake: local valve authority accepted. Remote override denied by route-integrity check. Drain speed falls when return corridor pressure rises.
en_US.audio: The pump does not save you. It buys time and makes another room worse.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Pump Room Handshake defines Submerge machinery language. The player reads a physical system, changes one pressure condition, and learns that repair is never free.
en_US.external_site: Pump Room Handshake is a gameplay-facing lore packet for readable pressure machinery: valves, sump logic, dirty feedback and the first cost of keeping a return route alive.

en_US.in_game_wiki: Hatch Seal Ledger turns doors into narrative machines. Each seal stores pressure, timing and route consequences instead of acting as a simple locked gate.
en_US.external_site: Hatch Seal Ledger is the door language for Submerge: a hatch is evidence, route blocker, pressure surface and moral record in one prop.

en_US.title: Cable Splice Scar
en_US.scanner: The splice is too clean for colony repair and too ugly for factory work. Atlas learned to keep power moving by hurting the cable less than the room.
en_US.field_note: Atlas repair should look useful before it looks alive.
en_US.terminal: Power trace: nonstandard splice accepted after human routing failed. Repair pattern repeats across later cable reefs with lower insulation loss.
en_US.audio: Something fixed the cable after everyone stopped asking permission.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Cable Splice Scar is early proof that Atlas repair is practical before it becomes biological. The player sees utility first, then intent.
en_US.external_site: Cable Splice Scar connects repair gameplay, Atlas behavior and cable-reef escalation through one readable prop family.

en_US.title: Sonar Return Route

en_US.field_note: Return route is a living cost, not a minimap line.
en_US.terminal: Sonar route: last clean echo invalid. Black Keel ping accepted. Local obstruction drift exceeds mapped tolerance.
en_US.audio: The way back is not gone. It is different enough to kill you.
en_US.in_game_wiki: Sonar Return Route defines navigation pressure. The player is not lost because the map is empty; the player is pressured because the known route decays.
en_US.external_site: Sonar Return Route is the navigation grammar of Submerge: return paths change, echoes lie by omission and safe travel becomes evidence work.
